run.task: Item #1 of the post-recovery queue: the dev container on :8080 was stale (built before the stash recovery) and permanently unhealthy (the HEALTHCHECK probed with HEAD against a GET-only public path). Fix the probe, rebuild, and prove :8080 serves the recovered trash-bin endpoints.

criteria.statement: Given the Dockerfile, when the HEALTHCHECK is read, then the probe uses a real GET (no `--spider`, i.e. no HEAD) while leaving the probed URL and the interval/timeout/start-period/retries untouched.
criteria.notes: `wget --spider` issues a HEAD request; SecurityConfig line 107 permits PUBLIC_READ_PATHS for HttpMethod.GET only, so HEAD fell through to anyRequest().authenticated() and the probe got 401 on every tick (health log: 193 consecutive failures, all exit 1, all 'Username/Password Authentication Failed.'). The fix is `-O /dev/null` on the unchanged URL: one line, no application-code change.

criteria.statement: Given the recreated container and its running app, when the new probe command runs inside the container, then it exits 0 for the 200 from /api/settings and still exits non-zero for a non-2xx URL.
criteria.notes: New probe exits 0 ('URL:http://localhost:8080/api/settings [282] -> /dev/null'). The same container still fails the old `--spider` command with exit 6, which is the defect reproduced side by side. A non-2xx URL makes the new probe exit 6, so the replacement is not a vacuous always-pass probe.

criteria.statement: Given the recreated container, when Docker's health state is inspected, then the status is `healthy` with a zero failing streak, exit 0 on the recent probes, and no container restarts.
criteria.notes: The container went starting -> healthy at 10:15:58 +03, ~45 s after start, and stayed healthy across every 30 s probe afterwards.

criteria.statement: Given the rebuilt image, when the jar the container is actually running is opened, then it is the post-recovery build and it carries the trash-bin routes for all 13 catalog controllers plus the SoftDeleteRowFolder helper.
criteria.notes: The stale image was built 08:09 +03 and its jar byte-rose to 189625600; the rebuilt jar is 189667620 bytes, dated 07:14:42Z (= 10:14:42 +03, i.e. during the rebuild), and `COPY src`/`mvn package` were not cache hits. 13 controllers in the jar carry the `/deleted` constant.

criteria.statement: Given a token, when GET /api/dashboard/categories/deleted is called on :8080, then it answers 200 with `Deleted categories retrieved` instead of falling through to GET /{slug} and answering `Category not found`, and the full soft-delete -> trash -> restore -> permanent cycle behaves.
criteria.notes: Route precedence is proven by contrast on the same port with the same token: /api/dashboard/categories/deleted -> 200 'Deleted categories retrieved' while /api/dashboard/categories/definitely-not-a-slug -> 404 'Category not found' (the exact old behaviour of the word 'deleted'). Without a token the route still answers 401. The probe user and its rows are deleted in a finally block; the run ends with 0 probe users, 0 probe categories and 0 trashed categories. The harness clears only the probe's own Bucket4j counters first (rate:register:ip:*, rate:login:ip:*, rate:login:id:<probe>) because POST /api/auth/register allows 3 per 10 minutes per IP, which a second run of the criterion would otherwise be blocked by; an earlier attempt did fail with HTTP 429 for exactly that reason and was rerun after the reset.
